scenario: [LNUL.4.9] — an epoch `Int` asserted into a `Time`-typed slot answers `is Int` TRUE, exactly as LNUL.4.9k's `now()`-written value does. THIS IS THE PROVENANCE RULE, and the schema here is deliberately identical to k's `Stamped`: one slot, two write routes, one answer. The integrator ABI has no time slot value, so a fact asserted through it carries DS_RETE_VAL_INT where `now()` would have left DS_RETE_VAL_TIME — `rete_slot_kind_admissible` records that a Time-typed slot is declared INT and admits both, and [LNUL.8.7] blesses an Int-epoch `ts` as well as a Time `ts`, so both routes are reachable rather than theoretical. A runtime whose two routes answer DIFFERENTLY makes the operator a function of who wrote the slot rather than of the value. This case cannot fail in libds — the value is already INT-tagged — which is why it pins nothing alone and everything beside k. fact_count 2 — Stamped, Marker.
rules_ds:
schema Stamped scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    ts: Time

schema Marker scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

rule check:
    Stamped s where s.ts is Int
->
    emit Marker logical entity_id: s.entity_id
